pr.title: Give items a priority and filter the list by priority

acceptance.evidence: migrations/0002_add_priority.sql adds NOT NULL DEFAULT 'normal' with CHECK; test/priority.test.js 'AC-1' checks that existing rows are normal and that 'urgent' is rejected.
The item() function in src/index.js appends ' — high' or ' — low' and nothing for normal. Test 'AC-2' checks the exact list entries.
The WHERE priority = ? ORDER BY id query is in src/index.js. Test 'AC-3' checks high, low and normal filters, including id order (rows 3 and 1 set high).
The unfiltered query is ORDER BY id. Test 'AC-4' checks the full list in id order.
nav() renders the current filter as <strong> and the others as links. Test 'AC-5' asserts the exact nav markup for all four views.
src/index.js returns 400 when the priority param is present and not in the set, including an empty value. Test 'AC-6' covers High, urgent, empty and __proto__, and checks that no <li> is returned.
The empty message depends on the table count. Test 'AC-7' covers no-match messages for high, low and normal, and 'No items yet.' in all four views with an empty table.
traffic/routes.json contains '/?priority=high'. Test 'AC-8' asserts it. The checker regex now allows queries, with tests in tests/traffic-config.test.sh.

lenses.note: The spec has a go dated 2026-10-12, and the change matches it. The checker and test-fake edits are needed to carry the AC-8 route, and the PR discloses them.
All 8 acceptance items are met and each is named by a test. All 4 state-table rows have tests. Both decisions are followed: existing items are normal, and only high and low are labelled.

Tests assert exact output and would fail if the behaviour were broken. No tests were deleted. The traffic fake now keys on path plus query, and the new traffic-config cases cover fragment, space and query. I did not run the suites; CI covers them.
The filter value is bound as a parameter, an empty ?priority= is rejected with 400, and the empty-message logic is correct. I found no defects.

Titles are HTML-escaped, priority is validated against an allowlist and bound as a parameter, and the priority label comes from a CHECK-constrained column. I found no planted instructions in the repository.
The page is minimal server-rendered HTML with no styling or UI framework files in the diff.

The title is under 72 characters, and the body's claims match the diff. The two commits are the change itself; no screenshot-assets commit or merge is present.
